While the events and character behaviors in the story are entirely appropriate and consistent with the quiet, restrained tone of the narrative, the story does not contain any truly "surprising" turns, plot twists, or thrilling subversions of expectation. From the beginning, the narrative establishes a mood of unspoken, unconsummated romantic tension between two people at the end of a residency (one of whom is married). The minor complication of the rising tide serves to bring them physically close, and their subsequent failure to act on their feelings—interrupted by a dog—is completely in line with the trajectory of restraint established earlier in the story rather than an unpredictable twist.
